name: Straight-Arm Cable Pullover
grip: Overhand grip on straight bar slightly wider than shoulder-width.
description: Sweep a high-cable bar downward in a wide arc to the upper thighs with softly unlocked elbows, isolating the latissimus dorsi through pure shoulder extension.
setup: Attach a straight bar to a high cable pulley and select the stack weight.
Grasp the bar with an overhand shoulder-width grip and take a step back.
Hinge forward at the hips approximately 30 degrees with a flat spine, knees softly bent, and arms reaching toward head level into a full lat stretch.
instructions: Pull the bar downward and backward in a wide circular arc toward your upper thighs by contracting your lats.
Maintain a constant, subtle bend in your elbows throughout the entire path (do not bend into a triceps pushdown).
Squeeze your lats firmly as the bar approaches your thighs.
Slowly allow the bar to return along the same arc back to eye/head height, feeling a full stretch in the lats.
cues: Pull with the lats, not the triceps.
Keep elbows softly locked at a fixed angle.
Hinge hips back and keep torso steady.
commonMistakes: Bending and straightening the elbows, turning the exercise into a triceps pushdown.
Swinging the torso upright and backward to yank the weight down.
Shrugging the shoulders upward at the bottom.

logging.example: Weight pin set to 25 kg: record 25 kg on that cable station.
logging.note: High pulley resistance and cable friction vary between single and dual cable stations; record selected stack setting.

variantNote: Standing straight-arm cable pullover using a high pulley and straight bar, keeping elbow angle fixed to isolate shoulder extension.
